reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
Originally, the Coconut White Cold Brew, a new menu item that I tried at Starbucks Bangbae Cafe Sageori branch last weekend, was good because it was new, so I was curious about other new menu items. Although it is not the closest branch to my house, it is still close, and these days, there are many branches with a better atmosphere, so I stopped by the Cheongdam Sageori branch, which is not as good as before, but still has a good atmosphere.

This Cheongdam intersection branch is located near a lot of entertainment companies. When I visited before, I saw Twice's manager, who wasn't a celebrity, but it seems like celebrities also stop by.

Among the new menu items that came out this time, I wanted to try something other than the Coconut White Cold Brew that I tried last weekend, but the other new menu items didn't really appeal to me, so I stopped by without much thought, but it happened to be a reserve store, so I looked at the reserve menu and there were new menu items. I asked the barista to recommend a menu with good acidity, and he recommended the Costa Rica Honey Process, so I asked for a grande size iced.

After waiting a bit, the Costa Rica honey process that I ordered was prepared in a store cup, and when I ordered the reserve menu, it came with two types of bark chocolate, which were nothing special.

Sitting at the bar table, I read the card explaining the coffee beans provided. I was told that they were processed in a unique way called the honey process for a sweet flavor like honey. I was excited to see what kind of acidity the coffee would have, and when I tasted it, it was iced, so I could feel the clean acidity, but not the sweet flavor.

I've drank it several times, but it may be because it's iced and brewed through a filter rather than espresso. Even putting aside the sweetness of the taste itself, I don't feel the acidity or overall impression is anything special. It's good to have acidity, but it's not impressive.

If the taste is this good, it feels much better than the coffee you get at good roasters cafes. Moreover, considering the price, I didn't think I would drink it again. I regret that I should have just tried the regular new menu instead of the reserve menu because the atmosphere of the store was comfortable.

Overall, the Coconut White Cold Brew that I tried last weekend was quite new, so I stopped by because I was curious about the other new menu items, but I didn't really like the other new menu items, so it happened to be a reserve store, so I chose from the reserve menu, but it was a disappointing visit because it didn't have the same uniqueness or the prices as you would at a good Roasters cafe.

reviews.author: delay
reviews.text:
The interior of the store was luxurious and the scent of coffee was strong, so I felt good the moment I walked in.

We each ordered different coffees, but the aroma and taste were all unique, and the desserts were also of high quality. In particular, the combination of croissants and coffee went really well.

I paid a total of about 140,000 won including coffee and dessert. Although the price was definitely high, I was satisfied considering the atmosphere and experience.

The staff kindly recommended coffee and gave detailed explanations, so even though it was my first visit, it wasn't difficult.
It was a great place to take pictures, so it was great to make memories with friends.

There are many types of coffee available as gifts, so I plan to visit again when I need to give a gift, such as on Teacher's Day.

reviews.author: English with Joy and Sinni
reviews.text: The Chanel of coffee. Decaffeinated coffee and croissants. I had chicken salad and they provide hotel-style service. There are many types of coffee, and if you ask for help, the staff will kindly explain. A separate stand is provided for bags as well. It is somewhat quiet on weekdays, but there is a wait on weekends.

reviews.author: byungho ahn (foodtrip81)
reviews.text: I went to the Basha Coffee Cheongdam flagship store, which started in the coffee room inside the Dar el Basha Palace in Marrakech, Morocco. Like the Hermes of the coffee world, Basha Coffee offers over 200 types of 100% Arabica coffee. You can enjoy coffee with classic dining menus and sweet desserts in the coffee room on the second floor. To use the coffee room, you must first register as a waiter at the catch table machine, but fortunately, I was able to enter right away without waiting. I've never seen so many different types of coffee in my life, but looking at the menu, there are so many different types of coffee that it's hard to choose. You can enjoy the original taste of the coffee at first, and then gradually add syrup, cream, vanilla bean, and sugar to suit your taste. Personally, I recommend enjoying the original taste of the coffee.

reviews.author: Su
reviews.text:
Visited on a weekday afternoon. I visited the store on the second floor to have a cup of coffee, but there weren't many seats available. When registering for waiting on site, there was only one team in front of us, but we waited for over 30 minutes and were finally given a seat.

When you sit down, you are given three items: a coffee menu, a dessert menu, and a booklet containing the history of Basha Coffee. The servers do not tend to give you enough time to choose your coffee, so I couldn't look at them in detail.

Compared to the overall high coffee prices, the bakery prices were not very expensive compared to other cafes/bakeries in Cheongdam, and the taste was average.

The overall atmosphere of the store is luxurious. The bathroom is really luxurious haha. I definitely recommend going to the bathroom too.
